newsitem.title: FINLAND: Broad rally, forestries, Nokia bolster Helsinki.
newsitem.headline: Broad rally, forestries, Nokia bolster Helsinki.

text.p: Shares rose on Tuesday in a broad rally led by U.S. shares overnight with further help from the strong dollar and hopes for a forest industry upturn after UPM-Kymmene's 1996 report and comments, brokers said.

The derivatives and portfolio benchmark FOX index was back above 1,000 points after Monday's slump and ended up 1.85 percent at 1,017.34 while the HEX put on 1.85 percent to 2,898.91, with volume a slow 465 million markka

Bourse engine Nokia, which made up 27 percent of volumes, rose over three percent or 10.60 markka to close at 307.60 after lifting back through 300 markka on Wall Street. Nokia is staging a road-show to investors in the U.S. this week.
But brokers said many investors were waiting to see reactions to Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's comments after the Helsinki market close.

UPM-Kymmene fell initially after roughly in-line 1996 earnings, but slightly promising comments and dollar strength lifted it to a higher close, up 4.10 markka at 108.90. It hit a 109.00 markka life-high earlier in lively trade.
"Speculation in forestries always starts once there is a slight signal about a possible upturn," one broker said referring to UPM's comments.
UPM said it expected a flat 1997 profit but CEO Juha Niemela said a profit improvement was possible this year even though the development was uncertain.

Engineering group Rauma, which also reported in-line 1996 earnings, eased 2.00 markka to 112.50, with some players expecting selling pressure as UPM plans to pay part of its 1996 dividend in Rauma shares.
UPM owns 73 percent of Rauma and said it planned to lower its stake below 50 percent.
The biggest gains for the second straight day were in mobile phone maker Benefon, which attracted buyers on Monday when it won type approval for its first digital handset model.
It ended up 13.70 markka or almost 14 percent at 111.90.
